decisions.text: type stacked_bar: a subtotal of several parts as an amount: a stacked bar, the summed parts adjacent at its base (G1.37)
one total, Donations, stacked from its 6 parts
stacking order from the base: East, Central, South, Int'l, West, North (the largest at the base, where it is read precisely; G7.31, D-26 (b))
each part in one colour and one place in every total: East (slot 1), Central (slot 2), South (slot 3), Int'l (slot 4), West (slot 5), North (slot 6) (G4.22)
one total: one stack, standing upright (07 §5.4), its parts named beside it: vertical stacked bars
6 values against 7 scale labels: whichever puts fewer numbers on the chart (G2.18): the values labelled directly, the value scale and its gridlines removed, the zero line kept as the baseline
value labels as a set, one magnitude and one number of decimals, the prefix and suffix on each: $133K, $72K, $60K, $6K, $4K, $3K (G6.16, G7.4)
each value before its part's name beside the stack: the text grey does not read on the parts' colours at 4.5 : 1 inside them (G7.4, G6.5)
the unit's description on its own line above the plot: “donations per region”; the labels carry its prefix, suffix and magnitude

each part named beside the stack, level with the middle of its segment, top to bottom as stacked: North, West, Int'l, South, Central, East; thin leaders to North, Int'l, moved off their segments to clear the others (their values before them) (G5.4, D-31 (c))
the title wraps onto two lines

source.shows: one stacked bar with three thin parts at its top, named beside it on thin leaders where they had to move (D-7); the book's inset on the top of the stack (G2.26) is a later stage for stacks: not drawn
